message.content:
For outdoor garden sculptures you’ll want a stone that balances **durability**, **carving quality** and **cost**. Here’s a quick rundown of the most common choices:

| Stone | Pros (garden use) | Cons | Typical price range |
|-------|-------------------|------|---------------------|
| **Granite** | Extremely hard, highly resistant to weather, erosion, and temperature swings. | Very hard to carve – requires skilled labor or specialized equipment. | $30–$70 per square foot (finished) |
| **Limestone** | Softer than granite, so it’s easier to carve with traditional tools. Good for detailed work. | Susceptible to acid rain and chemical weathering; can develop surface “pitting.” | $20–$50 per square foot |
| **Marble** | Classic look, smooth finish, excellent for fine detail. | Expensive, prone to staining and etching from acidic pollutants. | $40–$80 per square foot |
| **Sandstone** | Easy to carve, available in many colors, relatively inexpensive. | Porous – may need sealing; softer than granite, so more prone to abrasion. | $15–$35 per square foot |
| **Travertine** | Natural veining gives a unique look; fairly durable. | Can be uneven, may require additional finishing. | $25–$55 per square foot |

### Bottom line
* If you’re looking for **maximum longevity** and don’t mind higher upfront costs, **granite** is the safest bet.  
* For a balance between **ease of carving** and **visual appeal**, **limestone** or **sandstone** are popular choices.  
* If you want a classic, high‑end look and have a larger budget, **marble** works well—just plan for regular maintenance.

Choosing the right stone also depends on your local climate (acidic vs. alkaline soil, rainfall patterns) and how much upkeep you’re willing to do.
